title: God justified by men; wisdom justified by her children
source_text: II. Haec est proculdubio hujus verbi significatio ubicunque Deus dicitur justificari ab homine, sive inter homines, quod satis frequens est in Scriptura Veteris & Novi Testamenti. Sic Psal. 51. Tibi soli, inquit Propheta, peccavi & malum coram te feci, ut justifieris in sermonibus tuis, & vincas quum judicaris. Ubi justificari exponitur per in judicio vincere. Deus autem in judicio vincit, quum apparet illum ita sese erga homines gerere ut semper verax & justus maneat, sive puniat, sive misereatur, frustra vero profani de providentia illius querantur. Sic quoque apud Matthaeum, cap. 11. justificata dicitur sapientia a filiis suis, quia qui fuerant vera sapientia donati atque illuminati, agnoverunt & praedicaverunt summam Dei sapientiam in vita & doctrina, tum Christi, tum Joannis, splendentem atque elucentem, contra varias calumnias Scribarum atque Pharisaeorum. Qua ratione etiam populus & publicani, audito Christi de Joanne Baptista testimonio, justificaverunt Deum, baptizati baptismo Joannis: Pharisaei autem & legisperiti consilium Dei spreverunt in semetipsos, non baptizati ab eo. Ut legitur apud Lucam, cap. 7. vers. 29.
pass_a_gloss: This is without doubt the signification of this word wherever God is said to be justified by man, or among men, which is frequent enough in the Scripture of the Old and New Testament. Thus Psalm 51: Against thee only, says the Prophet, have I sinned and done evil before thee, that thou mayest be justified in thy sayings, and mayest overcome when thou art judged. Where to be justified is explained by overcoming in judgment. But God overcomes in judgment when it appears that he so bears himself toward men that he always remains true and just, whether he punishes or has mercy, while the profane complain of his providence in vain. So also in Matthew 11 wisdom is said to be justified by her children, because those who had been gifted and illuminated with true wisdom acknowledged and proclaimed the highest wisdom of God shining forth in the life and teaching of both Christ and John, against the various calumnies of the scribes and Pharisees. In which way also the people and publicans, having heard Christ's testimony concerning John the Baptist, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John: but the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, not being baptized by him. As is read in Luke 7:29.
pass_b_english: Wherever God is justified by men (Ps 51), the sense is forensic victory in judgment.
Mt 11: wisdom justified by her children; Lk 7: people baptized by John justified God against Pharisees.

choices.why: God or wisdom shown true, not made righteous.
